question.leadin: An uprising in this country's city of Timisoara (TEE-mee-shwah-rah) eventually led to the toppling of this country's dictator.
question.text: Name this Eastern European country which was led by Nicolae Ceausescu (chow-SHESS-koo) until 1989, when he fled its capital and was executed by firing squad.
question.clue: A dictator of this country who styled himself as "Conducator" ("con-doo-kuh-TOR") put down a rebellion led by Horia Sima, the Legionnaires' rebellion.

swap.leadin: The first democratically elected leader of this country was Sali Berisha.
swap.text: Identify this European nation whose past leaders have included King Zog and Enver Hoxha.
swap.clue: Its southern boundary is formed by the Pindus Mountains and its longest river is the Drin, which empties in the north.

question.leadin: While this country existed, it surprisingly boasted the 4th-largest army in the world.
question.text: Name this multi-ethnic Balkan nation that lasted from its creation after World War I until its dissolution beginning in 1991. It was notably a Communist nation that remained outside of the Soviet sphere.
question.answerHtml: Yugoslavia [accept the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes]
question.clue: This country's Partisans were led by a man who once sent a threatening letter to another world leader reading, "if you don't stop sending killers , I'll send one to Moscow."

swap.leadin: King Peter II called all people who wouldn't recognize the leadership of this man traitors, after this man successfully liberated his country from Axis control.
swap.text: Name this man who, despite being head of his country's communist party, split from Stalin and the USSR in 1948. He was a founder of the Non-Aligned movement.
swap.clue: Political opponents of this leader were sent to the prison island of Goli Otok during the Informbiro period.

question.leadin: This politician was overthrown in a revolt that began at Timisoara.
question.text: Name this communist politician who succeeded Gheorghe Gheorghiu-Dej and built the Centrul Civic.
question.clue: He originally came to power after the death of Gheorgiu-Dej, and is also notable for staying out of the 1968 invasion of Czechoslovakia.

swap.text: This eventual assassin of Franz Ferdinand was unable to act after the initial failure by Cabrinovic. He was imprisoned and eventually died of tuberculosis in his cell.
swap.clue: The failure of Nedeljko Cabrinovic ] to complete a task with a hand grenade prompted this member of Young Bosnia to carry out his most infamous action, after which he exclaimed "I am a Yugoslav nationalist" during trial.

question.leadin: The Byzantine Empire had many foreign allies.
question.text: The Byzantines received the support of these people during the 717-718 Siege of Constantinople under the leadership of their khan Tervel. The future Byzantine emperor Basil II earned the epithet of these peoples' "slayer."
question.clue: High taxes under this people's ruler Peter I may have prompted the rise of Bogomilism.

swap.text: This group's leaders perpetrated the Bosnian genocide. The country that takes its name from this ethnic group has its capital at Belgrade.
swap.clue: This people's mythology celebrates a man named Milos who walked into an enemy's tent under a white flag and then began stabbing him in the face.

question.leadin: Name these East European Communist leaders.
question.text: He seized Albania in 1944 and ruled until succeeded by Ramiz Alia in 1981.
question.clue: A vocal opponent of Mao (+) Zedong's "three worlds" theory, this man was abandoned by his closest ally, China, and successfully imposed state atheism despite his country's majority Muslim population.

swap.leadin: These two provinces were annexed by Austria-Hungary in 1908, despite that country having agreed to return them to the Ottoman Empire.
swap.text: Identify these two provinces ruled as part of a "Condominium." These provinces were annexed at the same time that Bulgaria declared its independence.
swap.clue: The Stanak assembly governed a kingdom named for this country, founded by Tvrtko I of the Kotromanic dynasty, until its 1464 conquest.

question.leadin: Ante Pavelic served as the Poglavnik of this organization from 1941 to 1945.
question.text: Name this fascist organization that ruled a Nazi puppet state from Zagreb. One member of this organization was known for keeping a jar of eyeballs on his desk.
question.answerHtml: Ustaše (us-TA-shay) [accept but do NOT otherwise reveal Ustaša (us-TA-sha) – Croatian Revolutionary Movement; accept but do Not otherwise reveal Ustaša – Hrvatski revolucionarni pokret; do NOT accept or prompt on “Croatia”]
question.clue: Along with the Nazi party, the Bigelow Report outed the Roman Catholic church for hiding this organization's gold.

swap.text: The Hungarian Revolution was partially put down by Josip Jelacic ("YO-seep YAY-la-cheech"), a military leader of this ethnicity. Nationalists of this ethnicity formed the Ustase ("OO-stah-sheh") during World War II.
swap.clue: People of this nationality received very little power over taxation in a dissatisfying agreement called the Nagodba, which did, however, allow them to elect their sabor.

question.text: In the 1880s, Austria-Hungary used this city's tramways as testing grounds for trams to be used in Vienna. This city was the site of the Markale ("mar-KAH-leh") massacres during a 1992 to 1996 siege involving the JNA.
question.answerHtml: Sarajevo [accept Siege of Sarajevo; accept Romeo and Juliet in Sarajevo]
question.clue: Concrete scars left in this city were filled with red resin to make its namesake "roses."

swap.leadin: It's not Turkey, but the term "Pomaks" is used to refer to Muslims who live in this country, whose Muslims, along with ethnic Greeks, agitated for an Ottoman occupation of Western Thrace in the 1910s.
swap.text: Name this country. Sixty years after abolishing its monarchy, this country elected its final King Simeon II as Prime Minister.
swap.clue: During the 1876 April Uprising in this future nation, Ottoman forces committed massacres in the Plovdiv area in this country's namesake "horrors."

question.leadin: This country's war of independence began a year after the Log Revolution and included the Vukovar massacre.
question.text: Name this country that carried out Operation Storm, resulting in the defeat of the Republic of Serbian Krajina.
question.clue: This country gained control of Baranja, Western Syrmia, and Eastern Slavonia during the 1990s under the Erdut Agreement, which was negotiated when this country was led by its first president, Franjo Tuđman.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about anti-gay rights movements in Europe.
swap.text: In December 2013, 65% of voters approved a constitutional amendment banning gay marriage in this Balkan country, which in July 2013 became the newest member of the European Union.
swap.clue: This country was merged with Slavonia in 1868, though Rijeka ] remained separate.

question.text: Liberals led by Alexandru Candiano-Popescu declared a short-lived "Republic" in this city in opposition to Carol I in 1870. Operation Tidal Wave targeted its oil fields in World War Two.
question.clue: After Antonescu entered World War II by joining his country with the Axis, this Romanian city became the target of an allied bombing campaign called Operation Tidal Wave to destroy its oil fields and refineries.

swap.text: The second Balkan war began at the instigation of Bulgaria because they wished to wrest control this city from Greece. This city was known as the second-city of the empire during the Byzantine period.
swap.clue: Several leading Young Turks belonged to this city's Dоnme community, the descendants of the followers of Shabbatai Zevi.

question.text: According to tradition, this was the name of the Serbian soldier that assassinated the sultan Murad. He is venerated as a saint in the Serbian church and is celebrated in the epic poem The Mountain Wreath.
question.clue: Unfortunately for Murad, he was assassinated by this Serbian national hero toward the end of that very same Battle of Kosovo.

swap.leadin: A king of this country controversially married Queen Draga, the former widow of an engineer. FTPE.
swap.text: Name this modern day country that witnessed the Slaughter of the Knezes in 1804 and the assassination of King Alexander I in 1903.
swap.clue: A leader of a secret society in this country codenamed "Apis" orchestrated the murder of its king Alexander and its queen Draga in 1903.
